overview: Numidian society belongs to North Africa's indigenous history and its wider Mediterranean connections. Thugga, now Dougga, offers evidence for urban life under Numidian kings and for its transformation under Roman rule. The spectacular Roman monuments there are later additions to an older town.

items.text: At Thugga, Roman construction was fitted into a largely Numidian street pattern. Urban continuity survived the change of political authority.
Libyan, Punic and bilingual inscriptions help reconstruct Numidian social and municipal life. Their study also contributed to deciphering Libyan writing.
The Libyco-Punic mausoleum preserves an important pre-Roman monumental tradition, although its modern reconstruction complicates interpretation of the standing structure.
Under Rome, an indigenous community and a legally distinct group of Roman citizens coexisted at Thugga. Cultural change did not require the town's earlier inhabitants to vanish.
